newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia unveils range of products at CeBIT.
newsitem.headline: Nokia unveils range of products at CeBIT.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy on Wednesday unveiled a range of new mobile telephone and wireless data products at the CeBIT industry fair in Hanover, Germany, the company said in a statement.

"With the introduction of our latest products, Nokia reinforces its position as the company offering the most comprehensive, broadest range of products -- not only for GSM, but also for the DCS 1800 standard," Nokia said.
GSM stands for Global System for Mobile Communications, and DCS for Digital Cellular System; both are mobile phone standards.
The new products, due to hit the market in the next few months, include three digital phones, a DCS 1800 version of the Nokia 9000 Communicator and two wireless data products, Nokia said.
"According to industry estimates, the number of digital (mobile phone) subscribers will double in 1997, from 50 million to a total of 100 million," it said.

"We firmly believe that the growth of the wireless data business will continue, and we see segmentation starting in this business as well," Nokia Mobile Phones president Pekka Ala-Pietila said in the statement.

"We believe that Nokia is well positioned to contribute to the growth of digital by supplying products to all major market segments and standards including GSM and DCS 1800, the Japanese PDC (Personal Digital Communications) as well as to all digital standards used in America," Ala-Pietila said.
Nokia said it had launched the following products at CeBIT:.
* Nokia 8148 handportable for the high-end DCS 1800 segment. Available worldwide in March. "We are confident that it will be a clear leader in its category," Nokia said.
* Nokia 8110i, an upgrade of the 8110 GSM handportable, incorporating a "smart messaging" feature that supports information services and Internet access. Available in volume starting this summer.
* Nokia 3110 GSM, with "unique" one-key access to functions. "We believe that the Nokia 3110 will appeal to both private and business users," Nokia said. Available in volume from June.

* Nokia 9000 Communicator for DCS 1800. Commercially available in April. The original Nokia 9000 Communicator for GSM, combining mobile phone, palmtop computer, fax and Internet access features) was introduced last year.

* Nokia Cellular Card Phone. "A PC card with a built-in GSM phone. This new product turns a laptop PC (personal computer) into a wireless office without a cellular phone, interface adapters or cables." Available in European and Asian GSM markets in the second half of 1997.

* Nokia Artus wireless data product family, including the Nokia Artus Access Manager and the Nokia Artus NetGate, which enable operators to become Internet service providers. "Both provide an Internet access point and fully digital, fast access to data services."

* Nokia Cellular Data Suite. Integrates the MS Windows '95 computer operating system with the Nokia phone, enabling the user to send faxes, receive e-mail, faxes, computer files and short messages via the cellular network. Launched for digital GSM/DCS 1800 standards and available in March.
